$comment: Central component inventory and lock set. This file is the single source of truth for
every external component CloudBurrow builds on. Reproducible builds consume the
'verified' versions here; #31 maintains it and tests 'latest-candidate' sets in an
isolated lane. A mutable tag may be used for discovery, never as the release pin:
'digest' is what a reproducible artifact resolves.

mode.verified: The pinned set below. Used by all ordinary, release and offline builds.
mode.latestCandidate: Discovered by #31, tested in isolation, never used for release artifacts until promoted here.

spannerEmulator.$comment: Google's Cloud Spanner emulator. Unlike Firestore, Datastore and Bigtable it ships as its own image rather than inside the Cloud SDK image, so it needs its own inventory entry — which it did not have when #37 was first closed, meaning `make deps-check` never checked it.
spannerEmulator.versionResolution: The digest was pinned first and the tag resolved from it against the registry's tag list, rather than the other way round: 1.5.58 is what this digest is, not what a tag pointed at when read.
spannerEmulator.licenseNote: The emulator's source is published under Apache-2.0, unlike the Cloud SDK emulators, whose licence could not be established.
spannerEmulator.redistributionPlan: Pulled from Google's registry by digest at run time. Nothing is vendored or re-hosted.
spannerEmulator.platformsNote: Both verified in the pinned manifest list, so the same digest resolves on Apple silicon and on CI.

measured.note: Measured on arm64 by running the pinned digest standalone and waiting for 'Server address: 0.0.0.0:9010'.

limitations: In-memory only: a row written before a pod restart is gone afterwards. Measured by TestSpannerStateDoesNotSurviveARestart, not inferred from documentation.

bigqueryEmulator.$comment: The BigQuery emulator. Google publishes none, so this is a community project, reused rather than written (ADR-0005). Since #1061 CloudBurrow builds it from source instead of pulling upstream's image: tools/bqengine compiles this module at this version, with the modules in patched replaced by copies of their pinned versions with CloudBurrow's patches applied (third_party/bigquery-emulator: sources.json, go.mod, go.sum, patches/, PROVENANCE.md). tools/bqengine's TestDependenciesRecordTheSources holds this entry to sources.json. Its fidelity is only what the compat suite shows.
bigqueryEmulator.notGooglePublished: Google publishes no BigQuery emulator; `gcloud emulators` offers none.

patches: CloudBurrow's: decodes the base64 of each BYTES value a streamed row, a load or a query's rows carries before it is bound, where the engine stored the base64 text as the bytes (#1065, #1075)
goccy/googlesqlite#76 (open upstream, by its author, unchanged): casts ARRAY elements and nested STRUCT fields, so a RECORD inside a REPEATED RECORD reads back after a stream or load (#900)

CloudBurrow's: keeps each table function's outer handle, which owns go-googlesql's finalizer, referenced for the catalog's life, so a garbage collection no longer frees a table function the catalog still uses (#1043, #1047)
CloudBurrow's: accepts and carries out DROP TABLE FUNCTION, which v0.3.1's analyzer refused ("Statement not supported: DropTableFunctionStatement") (#976, #986)

CloudBurrow's: keeps a FLOAT64 NaN, which SQLite made NULL when bound and when a function returned one, and parses and writes NaN and infinity literals, and an infinity inside an ARRAY or STRUCT (#1066, #1077)
CloudBurrow's: registers the unary minus operator, so -x of anything but a literal no longer fails "no such function: googlesqlite_unary_minus"

goccy/googlesqlite#80 (open upstream, by @cp-ant, unchanged but for its line numbers): builds a project's or dataset's sub-catalog without the builtin function set, which every catalog rebuild registered again into WebAssembly memory that only grows (#1057, #1017)
CloudBurrow's: addresses WebAssembly memory with unsigned 32-bit offsets, so a call past 2 GiB of engine heap no longer panics (#989)

bigqueryEmulator.buildTagsNote: golang.org/x/net v0.54.0, which v0.8.1 pins, leaves its HTTP/2 server out of a Go 1.27 build unless this tag is set, and grpc-go v1.81.1 needs it; with the tag the same sources build with Go 1.26 and 1.27.
bigqueryEmulator.redistribution: embedded: each CLI embeds gzip-compressed linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 builds and the licence and notice files of every module linked into them (internal/bigqueryimage); `up` builds the image dev.local/cloudburrow-bigquery from them on build.storageServerBase and loads it into kind.
bigqueryEmulator.redistributionPlan: Built by `make build` (make bigquery-binaries) and by each release from the pinned modules; no image is published or pulled.
bigqueryEmulator.verificationNote: Every module is fetched through the go command, which checks it against third_party/bigquery-emulator/go.sum (and the checksum database); tools/bqengine also checks each patched module's download and its files in the module cache against the sum here, and applies each patch strictly (no fuzz).

measured.buildNote: Both architectures from an empty Go build cache and a warm module cache, `go run ./tools/bqengine -force`, on an Apple M4 Max with 16 cores, Go 1.27.1: 2m08s wall, 404 s CPU, 3.1 GB of build cache. With the build cache warm and the inputs unchanged `make bigquery-binaries` does nothing (0.1 s). Two builds wrote byte-identical files.
measured.note: binaryMb is uncompressed, embeddedMb the gzip (best compression) the CLI embeds; both from the build above.

limitations: Single-project: it serves only the project given to --project, which CloudBurrow sets to the instance's default. Any other project is 404 'project ... is not found'. Measured, and asserted by TestBigQueryOtherProjectsAreNotFound.
In-memory: a dataset created before a container restart was gone afterwards. Measured. --database exists upstream and is not used.
Storage Read API: Arrow sessions work; an Avro session fails for any project ID containing a hyphen, because the emulator uses the project as an Avro namespace. Measured.
The Go client's accelerated reads (Client.EnableStorageReadClient, v1.85.0) panic on the emulator's responses. Measured; the raw Storage Read client works.
BQML is refused ('Statement not supported: CreateModelStatement'). DML and scripting worked in a probe but are not SDK-verified.

go.notes: Minimum language version in go.mod. 1.26 and 1.27 are the supported releases.
go.skipDiscovery: The go.mod minimum, raised deliberately rather than tracked against the newest release; the compiler releases are built with is goRelease.

goRelease.usedBy: .github/workflows/release.yml, verify and build jobs: setup-go go-version, so every released binary is compiled by exactly this Go
goRelease.skipDiscovery: Released on go.dev, not GitHub; the current versions are the .version fields of https://go.dev/dl/?mode=json. A bump changes this pin and both go-version lines in release.yml together.
goRelease.notes: The release pins an exact patch (#695). The other workflows still take the newest 1.27.x, so CI can run a newer patch than the last release was built with.

govulncheck.usedBy: .github/workflows/ci.yml, modules job, and .github/workflows/release.yml, verify job: go install golang.org/x/vuln/cmd/govulncheck@<version>
govulncheck.skipDiscovery: A Go module, not a GitHub release (the github.com/golang/vuln mirror's releases stop at v1.1.4); the current version is .Version in https://proxy.golang.org/golang.org/x/vuln/@latest. A bump changes this pin and the go install lines in ci.yml and release.yml together.
govulncheck.notes: go install module@version checks the module against sum.golang.org, so the pinned version resolves to one fixed source tree (#695).

sdks.$comment: Official SDKs, used only to prove compatibility. Pinned by go.sum.

goCloudTasks.notes: Generated contract types for the service CloudBurrow implements.

goCloudRun.notes: Generated contract types for the Cloud Run v2 adapter.

goGrpc.notes: Minimum v1.83.2: earlier versions carry GO-2026-6348 and GO-2026-6443, both reachable once a gRPC server is served.

goProtobuf.notes: Stable release; was previously pinned to a pseudo-version.

pythonVertexPrediction.notes: Read only to confirm the AIP_* contract constants and to evaluate LocalModel. CloudBurrow does not depend on it at runtime; deploy_to_local_endpoint is declined by design (docs/prediction.md).
pythonVertexPrediction.skipDiscovery: Published on PyPI, not GitHub releases; depcheck only discovers GitHub-sourced components.

goOAuth2.notes: Promoted from indirect to direct: the credentials compatibility test drives google.FindDefaultCredentials through it. Same version as before; no new dependency was added.

goSecretManager.notes: Generated contract types for the Secret Manager implementation, and the client the compatibility tests drive it with.

goTink.notes: Test-only (#416): the compat suite's envelope-encryption client for Cloud KMS. Never linked into the binary (TestTheBinaryDoesNotLinkTink); the server's crypto is the Go standard library.

goChromedp.notes: Test-only (#594): drives the console in headless Chrome in test/browser, behind the browser build tag, with cdproto for the DevTools protocol. It starts an installed Chrome and downloads nothing. Never linked into the binary (TestTheBinaryDoesNotLinkChromedp).

goTinkGCPKMS.notes: Test-only (#416): Tink's Cloud KMS integration, used as the acceptance client over gRPC and REST. Never linked into the binary.

goKMS.notes: Generated contract types for the Cloud KMS implementation (#309), and the client the compatibility tests drive it with. Promoted from indirect (v1.32.0) to direct. The server's crypto is Go standard library only (docs/upstream-evaluation.md, Cloud KMS amendment).

goNet.notes: Promoted from indirect to direct for h2c, which lets Secret Manager serve gRPC and JSON on one port. Same version as before; no new dependency was added.

goMSSQL.notes: Cloud SQL for SQL Server (#1916): internal/service/sqladmin reaches a SQL Server instance's server as sa, to make its sqlserver user, databases, users and flags, as pgx and go-sql-driver/mysql reach PostgreSQL and MySQL. Microsoft's own pure-Go driver; Google publishes none. Only its root package is imported (no Azure or Kerberos packages).

goCreackPty.notes: The console terminal (#781): internal/k8s starts `kubectl exec -it` on a pseudo-terminal, which kubectl requires before it allocates one in the container, as the session leader so a resize reaches it as SIGWINCH. golang.org/x/sys has no call that opens one.

goDifferentialPrivacy.notes: BigQuery differential privacy (#1455, internal/bigqueryfront/differentialprivacy.go): Laplace noise, the noisy count thresholding of groups, BoundedMean and BoundedQuantiles of Google's own library. It brings github.com/golang/glog (Apache-2.0) and gonum.org/v1/gonum (BSD-3-Clause), indirect.

goImage.notes: Vertex AI EmbedContent's WebP and BMP images (#1651, internal/embedding/image.go), approved by the maintainer 2026-10-19: its webp and bmp decoders. Promoted from indirect (v0.25.0, in the module graph only) to direct. It needs golang.org/x/sys and golang.org/x/text, already required at the same versions; no new dependency was added. Lossy WebP colours are converted as libwebp converts them (internal/embedding/webp.go), not by image.YCbCr.

go264.notes: Vertex AI EmbedContent's H.264 video (#1722, internal/embedding/video.go), approved by the maintainer 2026-11-17: a pure Go H.264 High-profile decoder (P and B slices, CABAC), bit-exact against ffmpeg here. Copied into third_party/go264 (import path github.com/cloudburrow/cloudburrow/third_party/go264; the module's non-test sources, fetched through the go command at this sum, with hwaccel_linux.go and its NVENC and VA-API backends left out and the import paths rewritten, third_party/go264/PROVENANCE.md), not required in go.mod: those backends import ebitengine/purego, which links libc dynamically into a CGO_ENABLED=0 Linux binary (TestLinuxBinariesNeverImportPurego), and a replace directive would break `go install ...@latest`. Chosen over go-avkit/h264, which needs Go 1.27 (docs/upstream-evaluation.md).

goMp4ff.notes: Vertex AI EmbedContent's MP4 and MOV video (#1722, internal/embedding/video.go), approved by the maintainer 2026-11-17: an ISO BMFF reader (progressive and fragmented files, avcC, hvcC, edit lists), pure Go. goOpus.notes: Vertex AI EmbedContent's audio_track_extraction of an Opus track (#1739, internal/embedding/videoaudio.go): a pure Go Opus decoder (RFC 6716 / RFC 8251; CELT, SILK, hybrid; multistream mapping family 1), standard library only, no cgo and no unsafe in the packages linked (its libopus comparison harness is cgo behind the opusref build tag, not built here), go 1.24.11. #1811 replaced github.com/kazzmir/opus-go v1.7.0 with it: opus-go (libopus transpiled) kept uintptrs to goroutine-stack variables and grew its libc shim's pseudo-stack by copying (kazzmir/opus-go#79, unfixed on its master), so a stack that moved mid-decode corrupted the samples (0.76 of full scale from ffmpeg under -d=maymorestack=runtime.mayMoreStackMove), and -race needed checkptr off for it (#1808). This decoder is within 1.9e-7 of opus-go's samples on every test track and its 5.1 and 7.1 downmixes within 6e-5 of ffmpeg 9's libopus decode at 48 kHz, and gives identical samples with the stack moved at every function entry (TestDecodeOpusOnMovingStacks). Chosen over thesyncim/gopus and tphakala/go-opus (both need Go 1.27; CI builds with 1.26) and pion/opus (SILK only) (docs/upstream-evaluation.md).

gav1d.notes: Vertex AI EmbedContent's AV1 video (#1731, internal/embedding/video.go) and AVIF images (#1736, internal/embedding/avif.go), under the maintainer's approval of media decoder modules (2026-11-17): a pure Go port of dav1d with an AVIF reader, no cgo, no WebAssembly and no dependencies, 8 to 12 bits and every chroma format. It replaced the vendored WebAssembly build of gen2brain/avif (libavif, dav1d, aom, libyuv), which could not decode a 10- or 12-bit AVIF over 13312 x 13312 in its 4 GiB of memory (docs/upstream-evaluation.md).

iso14496_26Conformance.notes: HE-AAC v2 streams with parametric stereo beyond baseline (fine IID and mixing B; IPD/OPD; 34 bands) and their unrestricted-PS reference decodes. md5 is ISO's own (mpeg4audio-conformance2ndEd_20230125.md5); sha256 was measured on the members downloaded 2026-11-19. internal/isoconformance holds the same pins (TestDependenciesRecordThePins).

realTools.$comment: The real tools compatibility.md's Verified real-tool rows name (#694). Test-only: CI installs or resolves them for the compat job, never with credentials; cloudburrow never ships or pulls them. A bump changes the pin here, in ci.yml or the test, and the versions in compatibility.md together.

googleCloudCli.usedBy: .github/workflows/ci.yml, compat job, storage, served, run and emulators shards: the gcloud, gsutil and bq tests in test/compat, through CLOUDBURROW_TEST_GCLOUD
googleCloudCli.skipDiscovery: Released through Google's Cloud SDK channel, not GitHub; the current version is .version in https://dl.google.com/dl/cloudsdk/channels/rapid/components-2.json.
googleCloudCli.digestNote: SHA-256 of the versioned archive, computed on download 2026-11-19 (its tar, gunzipped: sha256 5f80cdf432eefca57f6e3b1755229ee7339c46a6de7937fab124ba32e6529574). Google publishes a checksum only for the unversioned google-cloud-cli-linux-x86_64.tar.gz. 593.0.0 replaced 586.0.0 for `gcloud alpha source-manager hooks` (#1927), which 586.0.0 does not have.

hashicorpGoogleProvider.usedBy: The Terraform and OpenTofu tests in test/compat: every module requires exactly this version (googleProviderVersion in test/compat/realtools_test.go) and inits against test/compat/testdata/terraform/.terraform.lock.hcl, except TestTerraformRunServiceScalingControls, which requires 8.5.0 (the first release with google_cloud_run_v2_service template.scaling cpu_utilization and concurrency_utilization, #1802) and inits against test/compat/testdata/terraform-8.5.0/.terraform.lock.hcl
hashicorpGoogleProvider.notes: The lock file carries each registry's hashes for linux_amd64, linux_arm64, darwin_amd64 and darwin_arm64; OpenTofu's registry serves different packages, so its hashes differ from Terraform's. init installs the provider only if its package matches a locked hash.

scanning.$comment: Artifact Registry's vulnerability scanning (#1912): downloaded by `cloudburrow prefetch --vulnerability-scanning`, each file checked against these SHA-256s (internal/osvscan/pins.go holds the same values; a test compares them), and run offline. Since #1917 each release mirrors the four scanner binaries and the snapshots of internal/osvscan's Mirrored ecosystems as its own assets (release.yml osv-mirror, tools/osvmirror stage), and prefetch tries that release, then the latest one, before upstream; whichever serves a file, it must match the SHA-256 here.

osvScanner.redistribution: mirrored unmodified as release assets osv-scanner-v2.7.1-<os>_<arch> (#1917), with osv-mirror-NOTICE.txt (Apache-2.0, a copy in LICENSE); prefetch tries the CloudBurrow release first and the project's GitHub release after
osvScanner.notes: SHA-256s are the release's osv-scanner_SHA256SUMS entries, which match the assets' GitHub digests. Run as `scan image --archive --offline --all-packages` with OSV_SCANNER_LOCAL_DB_CACHE_DIRECTORY at the prefetched snapshot and every proxy variable at 127.0.0.1:9.

osvDatabase.license: mixed: each OSV record keeps its source database's licence (for example CC-BY-4.0 for the GitHub Advisory Database, the Go vulnerability database and PyPA's advisory database); the distributions' trackers (Alpine secdb, Debian security tracker, Ubuntu CVE tracker) set their own terms
osvDatabase.redistribution: Alpine, Debian, Go, Maven, npm and PyPI are mirrored unmodified as release assets osv-db-<ecosystem>-<sha256 prefix>.zip (#1917), with osv-mirror-NOTICE.txt naming the sources and their licences; Ubuntu (820 MB) is fetched from OSV's bucket only. Prefetch tries the CloudBurrow release first and OSV's bucket after
osvDatabase.skipDiscovery: A data snapshot, not a release: OSV rewrites each ecosystem's all.zip several times a day. The pin is an object generation of the versioned bucket osv-vulnerabilities, which keeps old generations for about a week, so .github/workflows/osv-pins.yml moves the pin (pins.go and here together, by tools/osvmirror bump) once it is three days old and proposes the change on a branch auto/osv-pins-<date>; each release mirrors its pins so they outlive the week.
